gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-006 concerns an invalid coercivity calculation caused by treating a variable coefficient as constant on control-volume boundaries. It does not diagnose the distinct mismatch between the set-builder definitions of the full spaces and the asserted interior-node spans, nor the resulting boundary degrees of freedom.

ISSUE-001 criticizes nonuniform constants and missing bootstrap control in a fixed-point iteration. It does not recognize that the advertised H2-wide Sobolev estimate is undefined because H2 does not provide the L2 gradient of the Laplacian or the stated L4 Laplacian regularity.

The gold issue concerns unsupported H3 regularity for the auxiliary solution under only a Dirichlet trace condition and the missing higher-order boundary compatibility. ISSUE-001 instead concerns uniform bounds and convergence of a nonlinear iteration, without identifying the boundary-trace obstruction to the H3 energy argument.

ISSUE-003 identifies a nonzero nonlinear pairing term when the scheme tests with the piecewise-constant interpolant, invalidating the discrete dissipation proof. It does not identify the separate definition of the mass-lumped quadratic form as a norm or the resulting false linear equivalence and ordinary-L2 energy derivative identification.

The gold issue is a wrong reaction coefficient in the auxiliary error equation: |Phi| squared replaces |gradient Phi| squared. ISSUE-006 concerns a separate variable-coefficient boundary quadrature/coercivity identity and does not recognize the incorrect reaction term.

ISSUE-006 explicitly identifies the failed coercivity calculation for A_h with a nonconstant Phi: the proof pulls Phi out of boundary integrals as Phi(Q), obtains a false exact cancellation, and therefore fails to establish coercivity. Its proposed O(h) defect estimate or constant-coefficient redesign directly addresses the same defect.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both the gold issue and ISSUE-006 identify the unjustified exact cancellation/coercivity identity for the auxiliary bilinear form when Phi belongs to the variable continuous space X rather than being elementwise constant. The coefficient variation produces a nonzero quadrature/boundary-integral defect, so the coercivity bound used in the error analysis is unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: The coercivity proof incorrectly treats the variable coefficient Phi as constant on the control-volume boundary, making the claimed cancellation b_h(Phi;v_h,I_h^*v_h)=0 invalid and leaving the coercivity estimate unproved.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that Phi is incorrectly pulled out at the single value Phi(Q), explains that this is only exact for an elementwise-constant coefficient, derives a nonzero defect, and proposes carrying an O(h) defect through coercivity or redefining the sampling.
